rv.q: This version of Bull teaches us that accessibility cannot be an afterthought; it needs to be at the forefront of style and stagecraft.
Sharp, darkly funny and deeply uncomfortable, Bull lays bare the human cost of a working culture shaped by competition, hierarchy and silence.
It may previously have won awards, but in a time of ubiquitous greed and corruption, I struggled to warm to the material.
Garfield's approach could make a stronger case for why Bull and why now, but the physicality that BSL offers certainly makes its violence more palpable.

cn.t: Mike Bartlett's brutal workplace drama remains an unnerving examination of power and cruelty, with Deafinitely Theatre's BSL production proving that creative captioning and sign language integration can be brilliant artistic choices.
